circuits.issue: Cable is 2.5 mm² as drawn; the specification requires a minimum 6 mm² copper cable.
The shower circuit has no 30 mA RCD protection as drawn.

sequence.action: Review the drawing and specification, identify all six final circuits, confirm circuit types, protective devices, cable sizes and RCD requirements, and identify the C5 cable-size defect and C6 RCD defect.
Notify affected persons, switch off the 63 A main switch, isolate the supply, lock and tag the isolation point, and prove dead with an approved voltage indicator.
Install or verify the main earthing terminal, protective conductors, main switch, distribution equipment and circuit wiring in accordance with the approved design.
Install C1 kitchen socket outlets using a 20 A MCB, minimum 2.5 mm² copper cable and 30 mA RCD protection.
Install C2 living room socket outlets using a 20 A MCB, minimum 2.5 mm² copper cable and 30 mA RCD protection.
Install C3 ground-floor lighting using a 6 A MCB and minimum 1.5 mm² copper cable; no RCD is required by the specification.
Install C4 first-floor lighting using a 6 A MCB and minimum 1.5 mm² copper cable; no RCD is required by the specification.
Correct C5 by replacing or redesigning the drawn 2.5 mm² cooker cable with minimum 6 mm² copper cable while retaining the specified 32 A MCB.
Correct C6 by providing 30 mA RCD protection for the 40 A shower circuit while retaining the minimum 10 mm² copper cable.
With the installation isolated, test continuity of protective conductors on C1, C2, C3, C4, C5 and C6 and record the results.
Test insulation resistance on C1, C2, C3, C4, C5 and C6 with sensitive equipment disconnected as necessary, and record the results.
Verify polarity on C1, C2, C3, C4, C5 and C6 and record the results.
Measure earth fault loop impedance on C1, C2, C3, C4, C5 and C6 and confirm the results are suitable for the protective devices.
Test operation and disconnection of the 30 mA RCD protecting C1 and C2, and the newly installed 30 mA RCD protecting C6; record the results and verify the applicable RCD protection.
Verify the absence of any required RCD protection issue on C3, C4 and C5, which do not require RCD protection under the specification, and record the circuit verification result.
Carry out functional tests on C1, C2, C3, C4, C5 and C6, including socket outlets, lighting controls, cooker operation and shower operation.
Inspect terminations, enclosure covers, labels, circuit identification, segregation, earthing and RCD/MCB arrangements; rectify any defects and repeat affected tests.
Remove tools and test equipment, confirm the installation is complete and safe, remove the lock and tag under the agreed procedure, close enclosures, and energize using the main switch.
With the installation energized, perform the final operational check of the 30 mA RCDs protecting C1, C2 and C6 and confirm correct restoration of supply.
Record all inspection and test results, provide the installation documentation and circuit schedule, explain the main switch and RCD test controls to the user, and hand over the installation.
